newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW -N.J. Blue Cross still hopeful of merger.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -N.J. Blue Cross still hopeful of merger.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Jersey said Tuesday his company hoped to achieve for-profit status within a year and then resume its stalled effort to merge with another Blue Cross and Blue Shield company.

Citing regulatory and legal delays, Blue Cross of New Jersey earlier Tuesday said it and Anthem Inc had mutually agreed not to extend the June 30 termination date of a merger agreement between their two companies. The pact was initiated in 1995.
But William Marino, chief executive of Blue Cross of New Jersey, told Reuters he was confident his company would eventually tie the knot with either Anthem or another "Blue."
He said Blue Cross of New Jersey would first have to prevail in its battle to convert into a for-profit mutual insurance company.
"My sense is we're in a yearlong battle to get through the judicial and regulatory process," he said, adding the company would then attempt to join forces with Anthem or another "Blue."
"There's a benefit to size. We can reduce administrative costs and have greater access to capital, which translates into a greater chance of producing lower premiums and better service," he said.

Marino said he preferred to merge with another Blue in order to retain the Blue Cross name and logo. "The Blue Cross name and mark are the No. 2-recognized name in the country after Coca Cola," he said.
Anthem, based in Indiana, is the Blue Cross and Blue Shield licensee for Indiana, Kentucky and Ohio.
But unlike its New Jersey counterpart, Anthem is already a mutual owned by its policyholders -- with the freedom to forge alliances across state lines.

Marino said Blue Cross of New Jersey would fight on in state courts to win mutual status, amid opposition from New Jersey Attorney General Peter Verniero and others who Marino said wanted the company to keep its non-profit status.
Although his company has lost in state Superior Court, Marino said it planned to appeal before the court's Appellate Division in September.
Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Jersey, headquartered in Newark, insures 1.9 million people in the Garden State, with point-of-service managed care to 860,000 people.
Liz Runge, an insurance analyst with A.M. Best rating agency, said New Jersey Blue Cross was one of many Blue Cross affiliates across the country struggling to win mutual status.

In a parallel with the New Jersey Blue Cross/Anthem scenario, she said the non-profit Texas Blue Cross affiliate has been unable to win approval to merge with the Illinois Blue Cross, which has achieved mutual status.
